prompt:
Refine image1, the complete Egyptian desert game map. Keep its entire composition, geometry, dunes, architecture, paths, central disc pattern, vegetation and warm painterly pixel-art style unchanged. Image2 is the exact required example of integrated material-colored edges with varied apparent opacity and pressure. Image3 supplies dimensional stone craftsmanship.

Specific correction: the standing stone columns and ruined walls are currently too pale and weak compared with the pavement. Give the structural masonry noticeably more weight through deeper warm side planes, stronger cap undersides, overlap shadows and slightly thicker selective contours. They must read as substantial stone with stronger edge definition than the flat path, without simply darkening the whole picture. Modestly increase contour weight, roughly 15–25% on the selected structural shadow/turning edges, NOT every edge, NOT a constant-width ring. Keep the clean coherent painted finish.

Assign edge color individually by material and local lighting:
1. Sandstone columns: honey ochre on light-to-side transitions, toasted sienna on shaded outer silhouette, deep warm umber below projecting caps and in contact gaps. Sunward edge cream/ochre, thin, low contrast, partly lost.
2. Rectangular ruined walls and rubble: earth-ochre on lit turning edges, muted reddish umber on shaded overlaps, deeper brown only in tight cavities. Vary along each stone, unite shared shadows instead of enclosing every block.
3. Pyramid and temple facade: golden sandstone to burnt ochre side transitions, warm brown recesses, deeper umber in portal/step occlusions. No black ink around masonry.
4. Flat path: quieter sand-beige/taupe edges with subdued ochre contact shadows, visibly less contrast and less contour weight than standing masonry. Do not bolden every paving stone.
5. Terracotta pots: warm rusty red and dark red-brown contours, deep burgundy-brown in mouths, orange-red reflected light on shoulders; blend as in image2.
6. Gold/bronze braziers and bands: golden brown and bronze shadow contours with selective warm bright rim.
7. Dark statues: blue-charcoal and muted indigo edges, small warm reflected highlights, not pure black outline.
8. Palms: deep olive/forest green leaf edges, reddish brown trunk edges, locally lost against neighboring shapes.
9. Central disc: sandstone parts ochre/umber, blue-grey inlays muted slate/teal edges, preserved ochre glyphs; do not redraw its design.
10. Sand: no drawn outline; dune boundaries built from related light and shadow colors.

The apparent opacity/strength of an edge must vary with ambient color, like image2: some boundaries merge into painted surfaces, others taper into short firm accents. Avoid universal brown, equal width/pressure, white piping, disconnected toy-like objects, noisy microtexture or global color shift. Preserve existing palette while adding weight specifically to structural stone. Entire map, no cropping, no UI, no text.
